title: Generate Binary Strings Without Adjacent Zeros
statement:
Call a binary string **valid** when no two `0` characters stand next to each other, so every pair of neighbouring characters includes at least one `1`.

Given a positive integer `n`, return every valid binary string of length `n`, each exactly once, in any order.
notes:
## Intuition

Listing all `2^n` binary strings and throwing away those containing `"00"` works, but it builds many strings that were doomed early. Build the string one character at a time instead: a `1` can always be appended, and a `0` only when the string is empty or ends in `1`. Every partial string built this way is still valid, so each finished one is an answer, and no work is wasted on dead ends.

## Approach

1. Keep the characters chosen so far in `chars` and the finished strings in `result`.
2. `extend()`: when `chars` has `n` characters, join it and record it.
3. Otherwise, if `chars` is empty or ends in `'1'`, choose `'0'`: push it, recurse, then pop it to undo the choice.
4. Always choose `'1'` the same way: push, recurse, pop.
5. Call `extend()` once on the empty string and return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 3`. From the empty string, `'0'` is allowed: `"0"` can only grow with `'1'` into `"01"`, which branches into `"010"` and `"011"`. Back at the empty string, `'1'` gives `"1"`, which branches into `"10"` (only `"101"` follows) and `"11"` (`"110"` and `"111"`). The result is `["010", "011", "101", "110", "111"]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · F) where F is the number of valid strings (a Fibonacci number, 6765 for `n = 18`): every branch of the search ends in an answer, and joining each one costs O(n).
- Space: O(n) for `chars` and the recursion, plus the output.

## Pitfalls

- Only the last character matters when choosing a `'0'`; check `chars[chars.length - 1]`, not the whole string.
- Undo every choice with `pop()` after the recursive call, or later strings inherit stray characters.
- For `n = 1` both `"0"` and `"1"` are valid; a single `0` has no neighbour to clash with.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `result` | every finished valid string |
| `chars` | the characters of the string being built |
| `extend` | the recursive step that tries the next character |

narration.3: chars holds the string being built, one character per slot.
narration.5: extend tries every allowed next character for the current prefix.
narration.6: The prefix has reached length n, so it is a complete answer.
narration.7: Record the finished string; every prefix built here is already valid.
narration.10: A 0 is allowed only at the start or right after a 1, so two 0s never touch.
narration.12: ...build every string that continues from it...
narration.13: ...then undo the choice so the slot is free again.
narration.15: A 1 can follow anything, so it is always tried.
narration.17: Undo the 1 before returning to the shorter prefix.
narration.21: Every valid string of length n has been collected.
